Our project explores solar illumination, sunlight duration, Earth visibility, and communication opportunities. We welcome team members interested in space exploration, coding, data analysis, software development, and 3D visualization.
summary:
About OFOQ

OFOQ is a project that helps us find and compare suitable places for landing on the Moon, especially near the lunar South Pole.

The idea behind our project is to make it easier to understand whether a location on the Moon is suitable for landing. To do this, we look at three main things: the surface, sunlight, and visibility of Earth.

When a user chooses a location, OFOQ divides the area into nine sections. This helps us understand the surface of each section and compare the different areas.

Our goal is to make information about the Moon easier to explore and understand, and to help users make better decisions when choosing a landing location.

Simply, OFOQ makes exploring and comparing lunar landing sites easier.
details:
OFOQ – Lunar Landing Site Navigator

OFOQ is a project that helps users explore and compare possible landing locations on the Moon, especially near the lunar South Pole.

The project works by allowing users to select a location on the Moon and view it in 2D or 3D. The selected area is divided into nine sections to make it easier to study and compare different parts of the surface. OFOQ focuses on three important factors: surface slope, sunlight, and visibility of Earth. These factors help users understand the conditions of each location and compare different landing options.

One of the main benefits of OFOQ is that it makes complex lunar data easier to understand through a simple and interactive experience. Its goal is to support better-informed decisions when exploring possible lunar landing sites.

To develop the project, we used NASA data sources, including LOLA for lunar elevation and terrain information, and NASA JPL Horizons for information about the positions of the Sun and Earth. We also used programming and visualization tools to build the interactive experience.

What makes OFOQ creative is the way it combines different types of lunar information in one place and presents them in a clear visual format. Our team considered important factors such as surface conditions, sunlight availability, and communication visibility when comparing possible landing locations.

Overall, OFOQ aims to make lunar exploration easier to understand and help users compare landing locations in a more organized way.
